newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: GOLF-STRUVER BACK IN THE GROOVE AFTER CLUBS' SWITCH.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-STRUVER BACK IN THE GROOVE AFTER CLUBS' SWITCH.

text.p: A seven-under-par 64 in the second round of the Dutch Open on Friday vindicated Sven Struver's decision to change his clubs three weeks ago.
His high-class round in high winds included an eagle and six birdies and carried him to a three-shot lead on 131.
The 29-year-old son of a Hamburg golf professional decided to change clubs at the start of the season with disastrous effect.
Even his father and uncle, also a golf pro, could not get his swing back in the groove and he slumped to an 84 in the French Open at the end of June.

Struver remembered his old clubs had helped him to a 63 in the South African PGA championship last year and a 62 in the German Open when he was still an amateur in 1989 so he decided to switch back again.
"I thought I needed to make a change of clubs at the start of this season," said Struver.
"But I just got gradually worse and worse with the new clubs, losing all my feel and eventually my putting, too, which was the best part of my game.
"When I shot 84 in Paris I decided enough was enough, pulled out of the second round and sent for clubs similar to the ones I've used all my playing life.
"I began with them the following week in Ireland and it has taken until this week to get my feel back.
"I've also got my putting back. I needed only 28 putts in the first round, 26 today."
Struver's nearest challengers are Englishmen Robert Coles and David Gilford and South African Wayne Westner.
